review_highlights.comment: I understand why some students have mixed opinions, but I had a great experience. She replied to emails quickly, and always sent assignment reminders. Exams are weighted high, so if you fail one exam majority of your grade goes down. Course wise it moves very quick and I would recommend you have prior experience in calculus or get started in it early. Exams are usually 11-12 questions. She's an okay professor if you have prior knowledge on calculus. If not, it'll be hard.

This class is pretty difficult if you don't have any prior experience in calculus, but the exams are all based off of the homework questions, so if you do your homework you will be fine. The exams make up majority of your grade, and only 12 questions, so you have to be sure to know how to do every single hw problem.

The only "annoying" thing about the course is requiring homework submissions to be both annotated and submitted via PDF, this isn't super easy for all students to do. Other than that, the Prof. was very accessible via email and for office hours. She had help videos up for all the topics.

Had Ms. Agud back in Spring 2011 and she was one of the better teachers I had. Lots of homework and it was randomly graded for accuracy. She was a tough grader at times. Long tests. I recall her mentioning she usually puts one or two tough questions on her tests and/or quizzes to "separate the A's from the B's" but I always thought they were fair.

analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Prof B is an amazing professor; he is genuinely interested in the material. It was one of my only classes I enjoyed going to every week. It is a lot of reading and there are group assignments throughout the semester but nothing crazy. Participation is a HUGE part of your grade so always try to engage in the lectures.
Really great professor, really cares about what he's teaching and it shows. Really good feedback on all projects and papers

Professor Burkette is a passionate and engaging lecturer. If you participate at least two or three times in the discussion for the day and put in the effort to skim the readings and do your part during the group projects, you'll see great success. Additionally, he provides extensive help during office hours, so I highly recommend visiting him then.

Took him for PSCI 3734 and loved him. He singled me out to praise a discussion post one day and we got to talking and now he is just as invested as me in my hunt for an internship. Checks in every class for an update. Amazing lectures. He was born for this. A must take professor! Flexible deadlines and cool projects. One of the best professors.

His Global Ethics course has a lot of reading and discussion. He does a great job of breaking down big arguments into simple ideas, is a little lenient with attendance, and keeps things fun. Grade: 15% 3 presentations, 25% 3 short ppr, 30% final paper (6-8 pages, double spaced), 30% participation. No tests. Put in the effort, and you will pass.

analysis.name: John Burleson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Only complaint is that homework had to be done in LaTeX and test were different than in class examples and practice tests. Lectures are pretty good, he assumes you already have a good understanding of Diff Eq. So sometimes he just skims over some stuff instead of going in depth. Pretty lenient with grading test and homework extensions.

Prof. Burleson was kind and helpful during office hours. I would recommend taking this online with Burleson rather than in person. This class is difficult (especially for non-mathematics students) and takes a very large amount of time. Nevertheless, if you put in the work (and read the textbook, trust me) you will receive a decent grade.

The best math professor I've had so far. The lectures prepare you well for the exams, and he provides a lot of resources to help as well. My only gripe would be the lack of feedback he gives on quizzes.

Burleson is a great teacher. He makes materials easy and clear to understand. He is available for help outside of class and he always answer the students' question. Very nice teacher. The daily 5 minute quizzes are actually quite helpful. It only account for very little of the total grade. Just a bonus, I love his silky smooth voice

Easily the best mathematics professor I have ever had. Had to withdraw from DiffEQ before to save my GPA. The first math professor at VT that I have had who actually had exams that looked like the homework he assigned. If you do the homework and actually try, you will pass this class. He is very easy to understand and works through problems slowly.

analysis.name: Dirk Buengel
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: He's clearly very passionate about what he teaches. If you participate in class and pay attention, you'll do just fine. He doesn't like the use of phones or laptops in his class either, so take note of that. The lectures are also quite long and don't directly tell you what's going to be on the exams. Use AI and the study guide to study for the exam
Tough quiz for every class, which requires you attend all the time. No computer or phone use, literally none. NO ROUND GRADES AT ALL EVEN BEING ACTIVE, EVEN ONLY LESS THEN 0.5 FOR NEXT LEVLE.

Professor Buengel is an overall nice professor but his Management Consulting is the complete opposite.    The class very seriously and provides very harsh feedback and requires students to be present at every weekly lecture. His grading is very harsh as he rarely gives students above a 90 in any assignment. There are better professors than him.

Professor Buengel is a very fun professor but he has quizzes at the beginning of class on the assigned reading, 2 exams, no HW, 1 individual presentation, and 1 group debate project. Outside of all that, his lectures are interesting and he really cares about your learning. He will also occasionally bring his dog in for class.

Extremely high expectations for the little amount of teaching he does. Did a poor job expressing feedback and getting on the same page as groups. Everyone I spoke with worked very hard and did not feel the grade reflected it. Rarely gave higher than a 90 on any assignment, moser averages were 85, but low was only 80. So do less work and get the B.

analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Bugh seems nice but is a poor professor. He assigns 100-200 pages of repetitive reading weekly from multiple books. He rarely uses Canvas, only for occasional announcements. Lectures are passionate but 90% tangents, and relevant material isn't on exams. Grades harshly on the only 3 assignments: midterm, group project, and final.

Very passionate about the subject but lectures can be lengthy (still informational). Lots and lots of reading for every class and attendance is mandatory, or else you won't understand the slides. Exams are hard but if you do the work, you'll get a decent grade.

Dr. Bugh is pleasant and he's not rude or difficult. However, he assigns an outrageous amount of reading (upwards of 150 pages a class) and his lectures are boring and not particularly informative. The class moves through history so quickly it's impossible to learn or prepare for exams, which are incredibly difficult even if you're studious.

Dr. Bugh is a great Professor, and I feel like he is the only professor I've had who has pushed me to earn every point of the grade I earned.  Usually giving 75% gets me a 90 or better, in his class you are "the master of your fate" as he puts it.  He has been around so long he knows how much effort you put in and your grade directly reflects it

Professor Bugh is an amazing lecturer. For this class, tests are short answer questions and will require specific detail. There is also a decent amount of reading. I think this class is doable if you go into it knowing what he asks of you. He also offers extra credit, this saved my grade.

analysis.name: Byron Tsang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: His homeworks are abstract and difficult to solve and requires you to really think, but he is available and willing to help you with it. The tests are easy compared to the HWs if you understand how to do the HWs. Overall, fairly easy-moderate class

Dr. Tsang is an outstanding professor who is very passionate about economics. The homework was challenging, but if you understood it, you did well on the tests. There is a group project as well that was a fun way to end the semester.
He is very nice and a nice grader. Tests were difficult to study for

Dr. Tsang teaches the material and grades based on applications, some of which you may never have seen before. It's a highly challenging course, but you do learn to think independently about the material. Prereqs 100% necessary. He curves a lot, so succeeding is possible, but homework/exams are very difficult and time-consuming.

This professor is great, he talks about extremely interesting topic regarding classical economics. The books read in this class are extremely interesting and Professor Byron is great. I would recommend.

analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Very easy class, especially if you study before each test. Graded only on tests, quizzes, and pop quizzes. He is very caring, dropping your lowest pop-quiz score and giving plenty of extra credit for doing school events. He is a funny and caring professor and if you just look over the material before each test you'll be fine.

Buddy is so kind and truly cares about his students. His tests can be difficult but he gives study guides and does exam review sessions before each exam. His lectures were engaging and he made us laugh. 5 quizzes (to prep you for each exam) and 5 "pop quizzes" (he hints at when each will be). He truly cares about the info he's teaching. Great guy!

Buddy is a great professor. Wants students to succeed, gives extra credit for meeting with him. Make sure to go to class and take notes. Tests can be phrased weirdly, but if you go to review sessions you're almost guaranteed to get an A. Does give pop quizzes, but in classes prior he tells you when they are. Very nice and easy to talk to. Love him!

Buddy is a great professor. You will be fine in this class if you pay attention and take notes. His tests can be weirdly phrased, but if you attend his review sessions you are almost guaranteed to get an A. He is extremely sweet and accessible outside class, and wants students to succeed. He gives extra credit for meeting with him. Love him

Howell is the only professor I've decided to leave a review for this semester. 100% recommend him. The class I took was extremely easy. His tests are very very fair, and he also curves. If you attend his classes, you'll ace all your exams + the pop quizzes (which are based on his lectures). He made the most of what a communication class would be.

People on here complaining about professor kennedy just don't give any effort in the class. she can be unorganized at times but she is a very knowledgeable and very kind. the class itself isn't bad as long as you show up to class and give a little effort. putting in the bare minimum effort will get you at least a C+. its really not bad at all.

Her class is all over the place. She never goes over PowerPoints related to the exams and just yaps about current events. She's also strict on participation, even if you have perfect attendance. She very nice though and gives extra credit with spot survey.

bro is genuinely the goat. He does do random participation speeches in class so attendance is sort of mandatory but he is such a chiller.
He is really good at his job and will often cancel class. As long as you show up and do all the assignments there is no reason why you shouldnt get at least an A-.
Very nice guy and great teacher. If you just show up, you will get an A.

Genuinely got teary-eyed on the last day of class. Martin is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. Freshmen, please take his class! analysis.name: Carrie Case
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Carrie Case was a very understanding professor who outlined her material in a clear and efficient way. Each test is completely open notes, and she encourages us to make cheat sheets. The tests have an in-person timed section and an untimed coding section. She offers an extra credit assignment that can add 2% to your overall grade. Really nice Prof.

This is just one of those classes where you have to pay attention and do the homework. You can't slack off, but I did really love Professor Case. I thought she was very caring and personable, she wants you to succeed. Her assignments were easy, you just have to watch the practice videos.

She's an engaging lecturer and tries to make her class fun. Personally, I wasn't the biggest fan of her. Homeworks and mini projects were easy, but exams seemed to be different than those. All exams were open-book and the final was online. She gives you 50 mins to complete the exams so it feels rushed.

She's fine. I personally didn't love her but ik a lot of people do. The class can be triggering at times with some of the statistics she gives (about death, cancer, fear, etc.). She talks about super deep and sad things with like no empathy. The class is easy if you go.

Ms. Case is so funny, has very engaging lectures, and knows what she's talking about when it comes to her teaching material. She cares about her students, and is very generous. All exams are online and open book, she drops the lowest homework and gives you two attempts. The R coding is simple and can often be copied from the module file.

Decent professor, goes pretty fast during lectures, 3 exams, does exam curves, attendance is mandatory

Professor Menegay was really nice. She goes over examples during class and the study guides really help for tests. The class itself is tricky so things can get confusing pretty fast.

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely one of the most caring professors I have had the pleasure of taking a course with. He wants his students to succeed, and he will work with you until you understand a topic you didn't understand. He is also a wonderful lecturer, even though attendance isn't mandatory, he explains tricky topics so well that they are easily digestible.

Dr. Nav is the GOAT. His lectures are incredibly easy to follow, and he prints notes for you to follow along with. He hosts a lot of daily office hours, which are very important to utilize. His tests are tough but fair, always covering exactly the units he said they would.  He provides practice tests, too, with LOTS of preparation for the final.

He's best math prof in VT, compare to who I have for calc 1 he is the best. Paying attendtion to the class, and respound everyone and check to make sure everyone is fully understand before leave the class. Host 4 final review before the exam, office hour everyday, and easy to understand. I got my confidence with him after last bad semester.

I had professor Nav for Calc1 & 2. He is an amazing professor in vt math. He prepares the slides for each lectures. He explains everything clearly at the first time which makes everything like hw and tests easy. He also gives a lot of office hours, which are helpful. His practice exam and hw are helpful. He posts notes which helps review.

Dr. Chathoth is a great teacher! I had no problem understanding what he was saying, even from the back of the room. It is a hard math class, however he is more than happy to work with you outside of class time if you send him an email. Only "issue" is we would spend the first 10 min of class going over last class, so we were slightly behind.

Candace Wall is someone who I thought I'd never encounter in my life, but looking back on life decisions, I can proudly say I am glad I did. Out of Eddleton, Wagner, and Wall, Wall is the best professor. That doesn't mean much though. She wastes time in class and speeds through lectures. She can be rude sometimes too. My advice is prioritize the studio worksheets and Aleks.

review_highlights.comment:
Very nice man. Infuriatingly bad teacher. I learned about 25% of the course from him. Loves tangents. Loves curves. Loves extra credit. If you're planning on skipping every class, he's your go-to. I went to almost every class and it was a waste of my time. 

My grade raised from a C to an A- from the final and extra credit.

You will either love or hate him. Does not work many example problems in class, and spends most of class going on rants and tangents, so be prepared to put in work outside of class. Curves every test, so your grade will be fine. I personally just didn't really care for his teaching style or his attitude.

100% would take his class again. HW took a long time but thats just bc the questions take a bit, not bc its a lot. He's a really kind prof. and you can tell he cares abt his students. Tests aren't too bad if you study and he curves heavy. He also helps w/ hw if you ask and responds quickly to emails. Plus his lectures aren't too boring for STEM.

First off you have to understand Statics is a hard course, anyone who had a bad review for Galitz just did not care enough to put effort into the class. Tests are heavily curved but there is a fair amount of homework. Has great lectures and is enthusiastic about what he's teaching. He does care about your grade but also that you learn the material.

Really amazing professor that wants to see you succeed inside and outside of the classroom. He talks through most lectures so you probably won't be taking too many notes. Try to understand the textbook homework as those concepts are translated to tests. Galitz gives you so many opportunities to make up your grade and learn from your mistakes.

analysis.name: Roger Chang
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

review_highlights.comment: Our Chang who art in heaven. Hallowed be thy name. Thy Statics come thy Free Body Diagram be done, on Trusses as it is in Total Bodies. Give us this test, our formula sheet, with non-numerical equations. Forgive us our mistakes, as we strive for partial credit. And, lead us not into failure, but deliver us from Hendricks. Amen

Roger is an absolute legend. If you can take a class with him you absolutely should. He cares about all of his students, loves to teach, and makes the subject very accessible. Lecture is easy to pay attention to. I took Dynamics with Roger 4 years ago and can still hear him saying "it's just geometry" whenever I'm working problems on the job.

Roger's class might have given me Stockholm syndrome. He gives 12 hours of torturous homework a week *minimum* and his exams (especially #1) are trauma-inducing. HOWEVER, he gives the best lectures at Virginia Tech and has 9am-9pm office hours. He will answer any question you have about any CoE class, and cares enormously about what he teaches.

Roger was a wake up call for my engineering. He gives a lot of homework (2-3 assignments a week) and his exams are tough. He does however care a lot about his students and made sure we understood everything there was to know about Statics. Going to office hours is key to success in his class, and he has office hours 10 hours a day every day.

Roger is actually the GOAT. I had him for statics, deforms, and dynamics. Many people drop his classes at the beginning of each semester because he starts by saying how hard his class is going to be, with the level of homework he gives, and no partial credit. I promise that if you attend class, listen, and apply yourself, his classes are a breeze.

The class had very few assignments, which became a double-edged sword in grading. Still, he gave plenty of time to complete said assignments and accepted late work for full credit if it was turned in within a reasonable time. He allows up to five absences before taking points off your grade. Just show up and pay attention to the lecture to pass.
